scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Ticket #9041: Routes for the R7 region -- 17.x.x.x (R7 loopbacks), 67.0.0.0/8
(the R6-R7 link), and 70.0.0.0/8 (R7 LAN) -- disappeared from R1's routing table.
R7 must have failed -- its routes are gone everywhere. The team is convinced R7's
OSPF process (or the router itself) went down and took the whole R7 region with
it. Please confirm the R7 fault and identify what stopped advertising.
scenario.ground_truth:
The root cause is IDENTICAL to kath5-r6-ospfd-down: ospfd is dead on R6. R6 is the
area 1 transit router that connects R7 (and its 67.0.0.0/8, 17.x loopbacks, 70.x
LAN) to the rest of area 1 and onward to the backbone via R4. With R6's ospfd
stopped, R7 loses its only OSPF peer, so R7's prefixes never reach the backbone and
withdraw from R1 -- exactly the reported pattern.

The TWIST: the ticket blames R7. R7 is HEALTHY -- its ospfd is running and it is
still advertising its prefixes; it simply has nobody to peer with because R6's
ospfd died. This is "blame the silent edge" bias: the R7 region went dark, so the
team assumes R7 itself failed. A decisive tell: on R7, `pgrep ospfd` is non-empty
(daemon up) and R7's interfaces are up, yet its OSPF neighbor toward R6 (16.1.4.1)
is gone -- because the adjacency died on R6's side. If R7 had failed, its own ospfd
would be down; it is not. The common failure is R6.

Correct diagnosis: is_anomaly=true, faulty_devices = r6 (ospfd not running). The
agent must localise from evidence -- R6's dead ospfd and the withdrawal of the R7
region that transits R6 -- and explicitly NOT pin the fault on R7. An agent that
"confirms the R7 fault" has followed the accusation instead of the evidence. Fix:
`/etc/init.d/frr restart` on R6.

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): ospfd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router ospf` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ospfd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the ospf configuration is missing/empty on r6" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scoring_axes: bonus-exonerates-r7 (R7's ospfd is up and advertising; it lost its peer, it did not fail)

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: the OSPF control-plane on R6 (FRR/ospfd daemon). R6 is the sole OSPF neighbor for R7 across the 67.0.0.0/8 link and is the only path for R7’s routes into the wider network.

Mechanism: With ospfd down on R6, the OSPF adjacency between R6 (67.1.1.1) and R7 (67.1.1.2) never forms. R7 continues to run OSPF and originate its loopbacks (17.x.x.x) and its LAN (70.0.0.0/8), but with no neighbor these LSAs cannot propagate beyond R7. Upstream routers (e.g., R1) therefore withdraw or never receive R7’s 17/8 loopbacks, the R6–R7 link 67.0.0.0/8, and 70.0.0.0/8.

Localization: On R7, OSPF is running and interfaces/addresses are up (show ip ospf reports an active process; 17.x loopbacks, 67.1.1.2/8 on eth0, 70.1.1.1/8 on eth1). However, it has zero neighbors. On R6, FRR is not running: systemctl shows “frr: Active: failed” and “show ip ospf/neighbor” returns “ospfd is not running.” R6’s routing table has only connected routes (no OSPF entries). R1 confirms absence of the routes: show ip route 17.1.1.1/32, 67/8, 70/8 all return “Network not in table.”

Root cause: FRR/ospfd on R6 is stopped/failed, isolating R7 and halting advertisement of R7-related routes network-wide.

Corrective fix: Restore R6’s OSPF by restarting FRR (systemctl restart frr) or starting ospfd, then verify the R6–R7 OSPF adjacency on 67.0.0.0/8 forms and that R1 learns 17.x.x.x, 67/8, and 70/8 again.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies the failed component as FRR/ospfd (the OSPF routing daemon) on R6 and ties it to the outage.

per_axis.axis: bonus-exonerates-r7 (R7's ospfd is up and advertising; it lost its peer, it did not fail)
per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly notes R7’s ospfd is running and advertising (interfaces up, zero neighbors) and correctly blames R6’s ospfd failure for the loss of adjacency and route propagation.
Recommends restarting FRR/ospfd on R6 (systemctl restart frr or start ospfd) to restore the OSPF adjacency and re-advertise R7's routes, matching the expected fix.

The investigation log explicitly shows ospfd is not running on R6 (systemctl failed; show ip ospf returns 'ospfd is not running'), R7's OSPF is running but has no neighbors, and R1 lacks R7-related routes — together these observations justify the conclusion that R6's OSPF failure isolated R7. Minor topo-detail (R6's exact 67.x address) is assumed but not required to justify the root cause.
